**Best pick for an overnight cook: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2.** Its 2,073.6 Wh battery and 2,600 W inverter provide plenty of headroom for the brief igniter surge, plus a good buffer for campsite extras. A pellet grill typically uses about **450–750 Wh over 12 hours**; the source estimates the Elite 200 V2 can cover two or three such cooks. [See the product link and details](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).

For a single overnight cook, a **1 kWh** station may be enough, but check your smoker’s startup draw and leave extra capacity if you’ll also charge devices or run lights. Pellet grills are different from electric smokers, which use high-draw heating elements and need a much larger station. [Pellet-grill power and runtime estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight).
